### **Summary**

Data leakage remediation and model performance validation via synthetic data pipeline configuration and optimizations.

**K-fold data leakage resolution**  
Investigation confirmed data leakage during K-fold partitioning from repeated file annotations. The team decided to resolve this input issue and retrain the top 2 models.

**Synthetic pipeline parameter optimization**  
Adjustments to augmentation parameters corrected silent errors that previously ignored critical processes. The team is addressing visual artifacts in synthetic objects and integrating procedural generation.

**V4 model performance metrics**  
Testing of the V4 model indicates an F1 score of 92 percent following class merges. Independent verification is necessary to confirm these unexpectedly high metrics.

### **Decisions**

## Aligned

* **Prioritization of K-fold bug fix** The project priority is set to resolving the K-fold data leakage issue, with Treasure Island inference and copy-paste augmentation tasks deferred until Friday.

* **Procedural generation testing strategy** The strategy for evaluating procedural generation is to use the existing train/test split to assess performance improvements while the K-fold pipeline is being corrected.

* **Data split parameters standardized** The team aligned on standardizing the data processing and model training to use 128, 256, and 512 pixel splits.

We've **updated the Decisions section** using your feedback.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Fix K-fold Bug: Identify and resolve data leakage in the K-fold splitting process to generate clean training data within 24 hours.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh, Ratul Shashank\] Support Bug Fix: Assist in debugging and validating the K-fold splitting issues.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Generate Confusion Matrices: Create performance evaluation tables for the top-performing model configurations.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Run Treasure Island Inference: Perform model inference on the Treasure Island dataset using the best-performing models.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Train V4 AUG Model: Develop a V4 AUG version of the model incorporating copy and paste augmentation.

- [ ] \[The group\] Create Image Game: Develop a simple tool to distinguish between real and synthetic images for testing purposes.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh\] Train Procedural Model: Utilize the previous train and test split to train a model with procedural generation included to evaluate performance.

- [ ] \[Pratyaksh Singh\] Validate Noise Augmentation: Investigate whether noise transformations should be applied selectively in the data pipeline to avoid artifacts.

- [ ] \[Ratul Shashank\] Test Problem: Analyze the provided code to identify the origin of the error and provide results.

- [ ] \[Ratul Shashank\] Share Fit Code: Update and share the fit parameter file once the code reaches a stable state.

- [ ] \[Sachin Pandey\] Document Annotations: Document the addition of UX images to the ground truth within the experiment write up.

### **Details**

*Did the screenshots in this section make your notes [better](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5bXzKQfylMIhSXc?entryPoint=multimodal&isGoogler=False&isBetter=True&confid=Tt4V9pNmKCTXYcss47XrDxIUOBEBMgUIigIgABgECA) or [worse](https://google.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5bXzKQfylMIhSXc?entryPoint=multimodal&isGoogler=False&isBetter=False&confid=Tt4V9pNmKCTXYcss47XrDxIUOBEBMgUIigIgABgECA)?*

* **Milestone 2 and Data Leakage Issue**: Sachin reported that an initial investigation into false positives revealed a data leakage issue during K-fold partitioning, where ground truth annotations were missing from certain images ([00:00:21](#00:00:21)). Pratyaksh explained that this occurred because specific files were repeated across two folds, leading to a scenario where a file had annotations in one fold but lacked them in another, resulting in training/validation data overlap ([00:05:25](#00:05:25)). Geoff confirmed that this leakage between folds is an input issue that needs to be addressed ([00:10:38](#00:10:38)).

* **Fixing the Data Leakage Issue**: Sachin estimated that it will take 24 hours to resolve the K-fold data issue, after which they plan to retrain the top two models from each configuration ([00:12:24](#00:12:24)). The team aims to have new results and updated confusion matrices ready within 48 hours ([00:13:41](#00:13:41)). Hemanth directed Pratyaksh and Ratul to support Sachin in identifying the root cause of the bug and executing the fix ([00:12:24](#00:12:24)) ([00:15:03](#00:15:03)).

* **Treasure Island Data Set Inference**: Geoff requested that the team run inference on the Treasure Island data set using their best-performing models. While Sachin noted that previous inference runs were performed on a base V4 model rather than the original K-fold split, they acknowledged that K-fold is not required for inference tasks ([00:16:38](#00:16:38)). Sachin and Geoff agreed to incorporate this into the current workflow ([00:20:39](#00:20:39)).

  ![][image1]

* **Copy and Paste Augmentation**: Geoff identified a requirement to train a version of the model utilizing copy-and-paste augmentation, noting that this is necessary to fulfill Milestone 2 commitments regarding synthetic data ([00:23:02](#00:23:02)). This task will be addressed alongside the K-fold data fix ([00:24:16](#00:24:16)).

  ![][image2]

* **Synthetic Data and 3D Object Appearance**: Ratul provided an update on synthetic data generation, noting that 3D objects currently appear to be "floating" because of a perceived gap between the objects and their shadows ([00:26:18](#00:26:18)) ([00:30:14](#00:30:14)). Ratul attempted to resolve this by adjusting pixel offsets but reported that this did not fix the visual issue. They are investigating other potential causes, such as alpha blending and the application of Fourier series to object outlines, and will provide updates as they work toward a solution ([00:28:11](#00:28:11)) ([00:31:47](#00:31:47)).

  ![][image3]

* **Synthetic Data Training Metrics**: Pratyaksh reported that training exclusively on procedurally generated labels resulted in approximately 50% to 60% recall on UXO classes, though performance on other classes like AOI support was lower ([00:33:52](#00:33:52)). Pratyaksh clarified that while the model struggles on the validation set, it maintains good precision and recall on the generated objects ([00:35:12](#00:35:12)) ([00:37:52](#00:37:52)). Hemanth suggested that combining AOI small black and UXO into a single metaclass might yield more accurate metrics than the current binary classification approach ([00:36:33](#00:36:33)).

* **Procedural Generation Integration**: Pratyaksh proposed integrating procedural generation and new augmentations into the existing training pipeline using previous train-test splits to see if performance improves ([00:38:46](#00:38:46)). Pratyaksh has refined the augmentation scripts to ensure that color and noise transformations are applied correctly without affecting empty black space or padding, which was an issue in previous iterations ([00:40:08](#00:40:08)).

* **Milestone Deadlines and Performance Goals**: Geoff clarified that the primary goal for this milestone is to show performance improvements over the previous iteration, rather than proving that synthetic data inherently improves the model ([00:42:26](#00:42:26)). The deadline for this milestone is the end of the month, which must include documentation and successful execution of the model on the Jetson device ([00:43:32](#00:43:32)).

* **Deployment and Pipeline Planning**: Regarding deployment, Sachin noted that they can run the pipeline on the Jetson similar to previous efforts, while hosting the Streamlit app on their local machines ([00:43:32](#00:43:32)). Geoff and Sachin agreed to revisit the deployment configuration over the weekend to ensure no blockers exist ([00:45:03](#00:45:03)).

* **Synthetic Data Engagement Idea**: Hemanth proposed creating a small application or game to share with the client, where users are asked to identify whether an image is real or synthetically generated ([00:46:31](#00:46:31)). The team agreed that this would be an engaging way to demonstrate the effectiveness of their synthetic data generation pipeline ([00:47:28](#00:47:28)).

* **Identification of Coding Bug**: Pratyaksh described a "weird" bug discovered in their code that had been affecting the training pipeline ([00:47:28](#00:47:28)). The bug involved the \`always\_apply\` parameter being passed as a probability parameter \`P\` in \`dual\_transform\`, causing the system to either ignore the augmentation or apply it with 100% probability ([00:48:44](#00:48:44)). This silent error meant that several manually written augmentations, such as poison copy-paste, were being ignored during training, which explained previous performance discrepancies ([00:51:15](#00:51:15)).

* **Strategies for Confidence in AI-Generated Code**: The team discussed how to better verify AI-written code to prevent similar silent errors in the future ([00:52:11](#00:52:11)). Pratyaksh and Geoff suggested using a secondary, independent AI agent—such as Claude or CodeEx—to perform code reviews and identify potential vulnerabilities or logical errors, rather than relying solely on the primary agent that generated the code ([00:53:42](#00:53:42)).

* **Agent Error Management and Workflow**: Ratul Shashank describes a workflow where they scope out functions and parameters using a "mind map" or "knowledge graph" to effectively manage and diagnose errors. By using this detailed context file, Ratul identifies connections to find the origin of problems and utilizes multiple agents, such as Brock and Lord, to resolve them ([00:58:08](#00:58:08)). Ratul agrees to apply this logical approach to Pratyaksh Singh's code to help identify the origin of specific errors ([00:59:52](#00:59:52)).

* **Agentic Code Review Strategies**: Pratyaksh Singh and Ratul Shashank discuss strategies for code analysis, specifically evaluating tools like "Understand Anything" and "Code Review Graph" to improve how agents trace errors. Ratul notes that creating a knowledge graph for code makes it easier for an agent to traverse the codebase, although the process is token-extensive ([00:59:52](#00:59:52)).

* **Critical Thinking with AI Agents**: Geoff Horowitz emphasizes the necessity of maintaining critical thinking when interpreting AI results, noting that counterintuitive outcomes, such as copy and paste yielding worse results, require deeper investigation. Pratyaksh Singh discusses balancing independent study—such as reading engineering books and watching videos to learn structures from senior engineers—with the commitment to contribute to T3 code ([01:01:15](#01:01:15)).

* **T3 Code Utility**: Sachin Pandey introduces T3 code, an application similar to the OpenAI CodeEx app that allows users to switch between agents and functions effectively on remote servers. Sachin notes that T3 code is advantageous over the Claude interface because it handles copy-pasting of images without requiring a subscription ([01:04:24](#01:04:24)). Ratul Shashank counters that while such tools are useful, the fundamental challenge with agentic tasks remains the quality of the provided context, as incorrect initial inputs lead to incorrect results ([01:05:48](#01:05:48)).

* **Parameter File Updates for Pit and Bulge**: Pratyaksh Singh asks Ratul Shashank about creating "pit" structures based on shared images. Ratul confirms that the shared parameter file contains ranges for both "fit" and "bulge," ensuring that existing work on bulge remains functional while accommodating the interest in pit ([01:07:44](#01:07:44)).

* **V4 Model Performance and Data Improvements**: Sachin Pandey reports that the V4 model, utilizing "copy and paste" and heavy augmentations, shows high performance with an F1 score of 92% when merging specific classes. Sachin notes the need to verify these results because the metrics are unexpectedly high ([01:09:06](#01:09:06)) ([01:11:46](#01:11:46)). Furthermore, Sachin improved the ground truth by adding approximately 80 "UX" items to the dataset cleaning ([01:11:46](#01:11:46)). Geoff Horowitz directs Sachin to document these results, including the confusion matrix and images, in an HTML report within 24 hours ([01:13:08](#01:13:08)).

* **XTF Data Format Technical Specifications**: Pratyaksh Singh and Sachin Pandey discuss the specific data format and processing requirements for XTF ([01:14:22](#heading=h.ly6f5flqqac5)). They outline requirements for split configurations, including 128, 256, and 512 pixel splits for training images and masks. The discussion covers the conversion process, including patching and preparing the data for the model ([01:17:53](#heading=h.hdjbpvmmqdgw)).
